findings.problem: RouteWorkflow uses flat booleans (is_validated, is_sent) instead of a typestate enum; callers can construct states where is_validated=false and is_sent=true simultaneously, violating the lifecycle invariant.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime logic observes inconsistent lifecycle state, leading to silent misrouting or double-sending; no compile-time enforcement of valid transitions.
findings.fix: Replace is_validated and is_sent with an enum RouteState { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } } and make RouteWorkflow hold RouteState; remove both booleans entirely.

findings.problem: status is String, allowing any arbitrary string value including empty string, invalid tokens, or values that do not correspond to any lifecycle stage.
findings.failure_mode: Pattern matches or comparisons on status cannot be exhaustive; invalid status strings silently bypass lifecycle checks.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with status: RouteState enum variant. The enum owns all valid lifecycle states.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a lifecycle flag that encodes workflow state without enforcing ordering; boolean alone cannot prevent invalid transitions like validated->draft or sent->validated.
findings.failure_mode: Code can set is_validated=true then later set it back to false, or leave it false while is_sent=true, creating illegal composite states with no type-level guard.
findings.fix: Remove is_validated bool; encode validation as a distinct enum variant RouteState::Validated or as a transition within a typestate machine.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a standalone optional field that can be Some(...) while is_sent=false, or None while is_sent=true, representing inconsistent lifecycle data.
findings.failure_mode: The sent timestamp is detached from the sent flag; code checking is_sent cannot trust sent_at_epoch_ms, and code checking sent_at_epoch_ms cannot trust is_sent, requiring redundant null checks at every use site.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the enum variant: RouteState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }. When not in Sent state, the timestamp is unrepresentable.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain constraints; any string including empty, duplicate, or malformed values can be assigned, and there is no type-level distinction between route IDs and other strings.
findings.failure_mode: Functions accepting RouteWorkflow cannot guarantee id is valid; accidental swap between id fields of different structs is possible; empty IDs silently pass validation.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype RouteId(String) with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and enforces invariants at construction; replace id: String with id: RouteId.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String for id and status, bool for lifecycle flags, Option<u64> for timestamp) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct invalid RouteWorkflow states directly by setting any combination of fields.
findings.failure_mode: Every call site that creates RouteWorkflow can produce illegal state combinations (e.g., status='sent' with is_sent=false), making the type's invariants unenforceable at the API boundary.
findings.fix: Replace the struct with RouteWorkflow { id: RouteId, state: RouteState } where RouteId and RouteState have fallible constructors (TryFrom / FromStr / smart constructors). Remove all raw primitive fields. mark_sent becomes mark_sent(state: RouteState) -> Result<RouteState, RouteError> enforcing the Draft->Validated->Sent transition.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent performance
no profiler data for hot-path analysis of RouteWorkflow transitions
no allocation analysis for String allocations in id and status fields
no second-ring evidence (no measured baseline vs new implementation comparison)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The struct has six fundamental Holzman/Functional Rust violations: status as String, two lifecycle booleans, detached optional lifecycle data, untyped ID, and no parse-boundary enforcement. A full typestate refactor is required before any delivery gate.
